history.en: Kshirgram is a village in the Mangalkot block of the Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal, famous for its Yogadya and Shiva temples. Banglapedia notes that the village's name goes back to the Kubjikatantra, a manuscript preserved at the Asiatic Society in Kolkata, and that the present temple was built around 1730 by Raja Kirtichand of Burdwan. The map pin is the village; the temple stands within it.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's right great toe fell here.

en: The village and its goddess are also mentioned in the Niltantra, the Rudrayamala Tantra, the Shivacharita and the Mangal Kavya.
Yogadya is worshipped with a big fair on Vaishakha Sankranti.
The Kshireswar Shiva temple stands a little way from the Kshirdighi tank.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.

nearestAirport.en: Kolkata (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport).

nearestRail.en: Katwa and Bardhaman are the main railway junctions of the area.

bestSeason.en: The fair on Vaishakha Sankranti (mid-April) is the main festival.
